edits.before: **Conclusions:** Matched-label comparisons distinguish the contributions of spatial refitting and support-only alignment. Their different effects across datasets make the update operation central to limited-label recalibration.
edits.after: **Conclusions:** Matched-label comparisons quantify distinct gains from spatial refitting and support-only alignment, providing a direct way to compare decoder updates with limited calibration labels.

edits.before: A decoder trained in the first Kumar2024 session must serve five later sessions. At the start of each later session, a short calibration run supplies only 19 or 20 complete labeled trials. Should these labels recalibrate the classifier, relearn its spatial filters, or update both? This practical choice links longitudinal motor-imagery brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) to the limited-sample estimation problem: each updated component must be learned from the available new observations [@lotte2018].
edits.after: Recalibrating a motor-imagery brain–computer interface (BCI) from a short labeled run requires deciding which decoder components to update [@lotte2018]. In Kumar2024, a decoder trained in the first session serves five later sessions, each with 19 or 20 complete calibration trials. We compare classifier recalibration, spatial-filter refitting and their combination using the same available labels.

edits.before: The matched-label comparison identifies a substantial spatial-component gain. Full CSP/LDA refitting added 5.47 BA points beyond classifier-only recalibration in the original primary cohort and supplied 73.7% of the mean total improvement over freezing. Holding the fitting examples constant gives this result a clearer interpretation than an updated-versus-frozen comparison alone: the available labels supported a useful change in the spatial representation as well as in the class decision rule.
edits.after: Matching source and current-session labels locates recalibration gains in specific decoder components. Full CSP/LDA refitting added 5.47 BA points beyond classifier-only recalibration in the original primary cohort and supplied 73.7% of the mean improvement over freezing. The comparison measures the value of relearning the spatial representation after the classifier has received the same calibration labels.

edits.before: The external experiment separates spatial refitting from alignment. With the same 20 current labels, ordinary full refitting was close to classifier-only recalibration, whereas support-only EA improved on full refitting in all nine participants. This places the original 5.47-point gain in context: its magnitude did not recur under the external data and implementation. An operation-level comparison, rather than a blanket instruction to update spatial filters, captures both findings. Acquisition, source budget, referencing and covariance estimators differed between datasets, so their individual contributions to this difference remain unresolved.
edits.after: The external experiment identifies support-only alignment as a useful additional operation. With the same 20 current labels, EA improved on full refitting in all nine participants, while full refitting and classifier-only recalibration gave similar cohort means. Together, the two datasets quantify the contributions of spatial refitting and alignment within their respective implementations.

edits.before: The neural extension adds a complementary observation. At the final support cap, fixed-source BN during full weight adaptation outperformed adaptive BN in both initialization regimes, with fewer collapsed seed/session predictions. This contrasts with the successful CSP spatial update. The component analysis distinguishes a supervised spatial estimator from repeated normalization updates, making the observed gain attributable to a specific pipeline operation.
edits.after: The neural extension separates another component choice. At the final support cap, fixed-source BN during full weight adaptation produced higher BA and fewer single-class seed/session predictions than adaptive BN in both initialization regimes. Supervised spatial-filter refitting and repeated neural normalization therefore had different effects under the evaluated support schedules.

edits.before: Positive session means and participant-deletion summaries show that its cohort average was not supplied by a single participant or only one point in the session sequence.
edits.after: The gain remained positive in every target-session mean and after every single-participant deletion.

edits.before: These details distinguish our information regime from reports using abundant target-domain statistics or continuous online adaptation [@adabn2016; @wimpff2025continual]. They also give a focused next hypothesis: when adaptation repeatedly revisits a short support run, normalization mode and exposure count should be controlled independently of label count. A follow-up can vary the BN update schedule while preserving the trained sources, support identities and comparison hierarchy.
edits.after: Reports using abundant target-domain statistics or continuous online adaptation address different information regimes [@adabn2016; @wimpff2025continual]. Here, repeated passes through a short support run link normalization mode to its update schedule. A follow-up can vary the number of BN updates while holding labels, minibatches and trained sources fixed.

edits.before: Matched-label analysis identified different useful spatial operations across two datasets. In the original Kumar primary cohort, full refitting added 5.47 BA points beyond classifier-only recalibration and supplied 73.7% of the total mean gain over freezing. In BNCI2014-001, full refitting was close to classifier-only recalibration, while support-only EA added 5.65 points beyond full refitting and improved all nine participants. Short-run recalibration should therefore compare the spatial update itself under identical labels. Fixed source normalization reduced single-class neural predictions at the 20-label cap; complete budget profiles and strong geometric references delimit the additional mechanism results.
edits.after: Matched-label analysis quantified gains from two spatial operations during short-run recalibration. In the original Kumar primary cohort, full refitting added 5.47 BA points beyond classifier-only recalibration and supplied 73.7% of the mean total gain over freezing. In BNCI2014-001, support-only EA added 5.65 points beyond full refitting, with improvement in all nine participants; full refitting and classifier-only recalibration gave similar cohort means. Fixed source normalization reduced single-class neural predictions at the 20-label cap. These component comparisons provide a direct way to evaluate how a short calibration run should update the decoder.
